passage:
Nilesh was folding laundry in the flat when a friend's name kept scrolling past on the screen: Tarun. A joke Tarun had posted last week, clipped and stripped of context, had become hundreds of angry replies. People were demanding that his college expel him. Nilesh's thumb hovered over "reply" to defend him publicly. Nilesh's stomach tightened: what if the crowd came for Nilesh next?

Nilesh put the phone down, breathed, and picked it up again. No public reply. A private message instead: "I saw it. I'm with you. Want to report the worst ones together?"

Tarun answered in ten seconds: "Yes. I feel sick."

They spent an hour reporting threats. Two days later, when the anger had thinned, Nilesh posted: "Tarun is a friend. The clip leaves out the rest."

qa.q: What did Nilesh send Tarun privately?
qa.a: Nilesh sent, "I saw it. I'm with you. Want to report the worst ones together?"

qa.q: What was Nilesh afraid of while deciding whether to reply?
qa.a: Nilesh feared the crowd would come for Nilesh next, so Nilesh's stomach tightened while the thumb hovered over "reply".

qa.q: Why was messaging privately first a good move?
qa.a: It supported Tarun right away and helped report threats without putting Nilesh in the crowd's sights, and Nilesh spoke up publicly later when it was safer.

qa.q: How might Tarun have felt when Nilesh's message arrived?
qa.a: Tarun felt sick but answered within ten seconds with a yes, which suggests relief at not being alone.

grounding: Nilesh wants to defend a mobbed friend but fears being targeted, so reaches out privately first, helps him report and speaks up when safer.

passage:
Zubin: bro I saw the thread about your stall. you ok?
Akash: no
Akash: 1 bad review and now 5000 people saying I poisoned someone
Akash: I didn't. the guy ate there 2 weeks ago
Zubin: I know you didn't
Zubin: honestly I was scared to comment. they're going after anyone defending you
Zubin: but I'm not leaving you alone in this
Akash: thanks yaar. I can't eat
Zubin: let's report the posts with your address first. then your dad can talk to the market association
Akash: ok. can you come by
Zubin: leaving now

That evening Zubin posted on his own page: "I've eaten at Akash's stall for two years. Check facts before sharing." A few people unfollowed him. Akash sent a heart.

qa.q: How many people were saying Akash poisoned someone?
qa.a: About 5000 people were saying Akash poisoned someone.

qa.q: What was Zubin worried about before commenting?
qa.a: Zubin was scared that the mob would go after Zubin too, because they were attacking anyone defending Akash.

qa.q: What did Zubin do first, and why was that a good order?
qa.a: Zubin reached out privately and helped report the posts with Akash's address first, so safety came before a public statement.

qa.q: How might Akash have felt when Zubin posted publicly?
qa.a: Akash likely felt less alone and grateful, since a friend chose to stand beside him even though it cost some followers.

grounding: The chat shows a young person afraid of being targeted who reaches out privately, helps his friend report, and speaks up publicly once safe.

passage:
In Karnal the news spread fast. Someone had filmed Sumit arguing with a customer at his father's mobile repair shop and posted it with the caption "thief". By noon the town page had hundreds of comments, and a few mentioned the shop's address.

Harish saw it on the tractor ride back from the fields. His thumb hovered over the comment box. If he defended Sumit, his own photos would be dragged in. He put the phone away.

At home his sister Gargi looked up from her books. "You've gone quiet. Is it Sumit?" He nodded.

"Then go and see him. You don't have to fight the whole town today."

Harish rode to the shop. He helped Sumit and his father report the posts that showed the address, and stayed until they closed. Two days later, when things had cooled, he wrote under the video that the customer had left without paying.

qa.q: What caption was posted with the video of Sumit?
qa.a: The video was posted with the caption "thief".

qa.q: Why did Harish put his phone away on the tractor ride?
qa.a: Harish was afraid that if he defended Sumit, his own photos would be dragged in, so fear held him back even though he cared.

qa.q: How did Gargi's advice help Harish choose a better path?
qa.a: Gargi suggested going to see Sumit instead of fighting the whole town, so Harish supported his friend in person and spoke up later when it was calmer.

qa.q: How might Sumit have felt when Harish arrived at the shop?
qa.a: Sumit probably felt relieved and less alone, seeing a friend show up while strangers were attacking him.

grounding: The story shows a young man torn between loyalty and fear who supports his mobbed friend privately first and speaks up when it is safer.
